title: Alphabet Earnings Miss Estimates as EPS Falls to $2.12 Despite Revenue Rising 25% to $127.6 Billion
excerpt: Alphabet's operating income rose 30% and Google Cloud revenue doubled, but an $8.7 billion equity-securities loss and $51.4 billion of capital spending pushed EPS and free cash flow below expectations.
body:
• Alphabet missed estimates on both lines in the third quarter: revenue rose 25% to $127.58 billion, just short of about $127.96 billion expected, and diluted earnings fell to $2.12 per share against $3.02 expected.
  • The operating business grew strongly — operating income rose 30% to $40.58 billion — but an $8.7 billion loss on equity securities cut net income by $6.7 billion and EPS by $0.55, pulling reported profit down 25%.
  • Google Cloud was the standout: revenue more than doubled, up 103% to $30.71 billion, with operating income tripling to $11.12 billion and a $561 billion backlog.
  • Capital spending of $51.36 billion outran operating cash flow of $42.29 billion, leaving free cash flow at negative $9.07 billion for a second straight quarter — the figure that drove a roughly 10% after-hours fall.

Alphabet delivered a split verdict on Wednesday: a fast-growing operating business and a headline miss. The Google parent reported third-quarter revenue of $127.58 billion for the quarter ended September 30, up 25% from $102.35 billion a year earlier and its 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, but just below Wall Street expectations.

An investment loss, not an operating slump, drove the EPS miss

Operating income rose 30% to $40.58 billion, with the operating margin widening to 31.8% from 31% a year earlier. The damage sat below that line. Other income swung to an $8.22 billion expense from $12.76 billion of income a year earlier, driven by an $8.66 billion net loss on equity securities — against a $10.73 billion gain in the prior-year quarter. Alphabet said that loss reduced net income by $6.7 billion and diluted earnings per share by $0.55.

Net income available to common stockholders fell 25% to $26.17 billion, and diluted EPS fell to $2.12 from $2.87 a year earlier, missing the $3.02 consensus compiled by market data providers and the $2.94 Zacks consensus. Zacks noted revenues excluding traffic acquisition costs rose 27% to $111.21 billion, still slightly short of its consensus.

Cloud doubles; Search grows more slowly

Google Cloud revenue surged 103% to $30.71 billion, ahead of estimates, as enterprise demand for AI infrastructure and AI solutions — including sales of Alphabet's own TPU systems — lifted the segment. Cloud operating income rose to $11.12 billion from $3.59 billion, and Zacks put the Cloud backlog at $561 billion.

Google Services, the larger business, grew more modestly. Revenue rose 11% to $96.30 billion, with Search and other revenue up 12% to $63.35 billion on what the company called the highest query growth rate in five years. YouTube advertising revenue rose 9% to $11.21 billion, Google Network revenue edged up 1% to $7.46 billion, and subscriptions, platforms and devices revenue rose 11% to $14.29 billion. Services operating income rose 17% to $39.16 billion. Other Bets revenue was $372 million with a wider operating loss of $2.05 billion.

"Google Cloud revenues grew 103%, powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions."

— Sundar Pichai, Chief Executive Officer, Alphabet and Google

The cash-flow line is what the market punished

Capital expenditure more than doubled to $51.36 billion in the quarter, exceeding operating cash flow of $42.29 billion. Free cash flow was negative $9.07 billion, a second consecutive negative quarter, and far weaker than investors expected. Alphabet funded the gap in part from capital markets, issuing about $28.7 billion of senior notes and roughly $12.4 billion of stock during the quarter, and bought back no shares. Management kept full-year 2026 capital spending guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion and said spending will increase significantly in 2027.

What comes next

Shares fell about 10% in after-hours trading, putting the stock on course for one of its largest post-earnings drops, even as Cloud growth accelerated. The debate is now narrow and financial: whether Cloud's profit growth — operating income up more than 200% — can outrun a capital program that is consuming more cash than operations generate. Alphabet will pay a $0.22 per share dividend on Class A, B and C stock on December 14 to holders registered on December 7, according to the release. The next test is the holiday quarter, where Search and Cloud conversion will decide the spending case.
